prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and for the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: After reading all eight first-round statements and the chair's summary, I keep B047 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as my single-part configuration. The reasons are unchanged and have been tested by the exchange. Kane and Mele showed that a time-reversal-invariant insulator with spin-orbit coupling carries a Z2 invariant instead of a broken symmetry, and that this invariant has a measurable consequence, namely protected helical edge transport. Molenkamp's group then observed that edge conductance in HgTe/CdTe wells. That is a prediction followed by a direct experimental test, and the interpretation has held for fifteen years or more across many materials. Eriksson and Mehlig reach the same configuration from different starting points, and the chair records that none of the B010 or B051 supporters rejects B047 on merit. I regard the science as mature. What remains open is the credit, and I would handle that in the citation wording and in the record, not by changing the names to buy agreement. My preferred configuration is therefore unchanged from round 1. The one change is among my alternatives: I replace B041 with B010. The chair's summary shows B041 is a poor choice this year for several of us, and I will not argue for it given my position at Chalmers and WACQT. B010 is now the more informative alternative because it is where the largest group of colleagues stands.
statement.case_against: The credit weakness remains and I cannot argue it away. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route that Molenkamp realised, Zhang cannot be recognised, and the three-dimensional work of Hasan, Fu and Moore falls outside a three-name cap. The 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions is adjacent, and the committee has to be willing to say in one sentence why the Z2 insulator is a distinct discovery. My answer is that the 2016 prize concerned topological order in model systems, namely the integer quantum Hall plateaus, the Haldane chain and the defect-mediated transition. B047 concerns a time-reversal-symmetric, spin-orbit-driven phase of real materials with no magnetic field. Several colleagues, including Olsson and Kroll, may judge this insufficient, and that is a legitimate difference of judgement. Against B010 specifically: it has the cleanest credit and a strong measurement record, so if the committee gives measurement capability the same weight as a new organising concept, then B010 may deserve to win. If the allocation for B047 truly cannot be settled, B046 remains a clean pair, though it has little support in the room.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B010 for Katori and Ye, arguing that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct invention from the 2005 comb and the 2012 ion-control prizes, that the credit boundary is the cleanest on the shortlist, and that the step change in measurement capability is already producing new tests.
responses.response: The chair asks whether the magic-wavelength framing answers my novelty objection. Partly. I accept that cancelling the trap-induced light shift at a magic wavelength is a specific idea that the comb and ion-trap work did not supply, and that it is a more precise ground than 'optical clocks' in general. That removes my strongest objection, and I withdraw the suggestion that the toolbox was already recognised. What I still weigh differently is the kind of achievement. The lattice clock is a step in measurement accuracy whose largest consequences, such as the redefinition of the second and constant-variation limits, are mostly prospective, while B047 changed how a class of materials is classified. I do not think that difference is decisive, and I would not oppose B010 as a part of a two-part prize or as the committee's choice if the majority weighs capability as you do. I would ask you to say plainly in the citation that ion-clock groups and other lattice-clock teams fall outside the credit.

responses.point: Lindroth prefers B010, says neither attribution nor maturity is seriously in doubt, and acknowledges that B047 has more top-three placements while B051 has a higher Borda total, but would not lean on the pending redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree with you that the pending redefinition should stay out of the citation, and that B010 is one of the few candidates where credit and maturity are both comfortable. I take that as a real advantage over B047, where I admit maturity of the science is secure but maturity of the credit is not. Where we differ is on the weighing question in the chair's list. You describe the accuracy improvement as the achievement. I read the Kane-Mele result as the discovery of a new organising principle plus a materials realisation, and I put that above an accuracy record, though the gap is a matter of taste and I do not claim it is a scientific fact. I also note that you list B047 as your first alternative and I list B010 as mine, so our positions are close, and the vote may come down to which criterion the majority prefers.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B047, treats the Z2 classification as a conceptual change, and raises a combined two-part configuration of B047 with a precision or quantum-technology achievement as a possibly fairer outcome.
responses.response: I agree on the concept and on keeping Mele. On the two-part idea, I considered it. A two-part prize pairing B047 with B010 would respect the criterion held by the B010 group without lowering the standard for either part, and the chair notes that you and Danielsson would not oppose such a result. My concern is that the cap of three unique people across the configuration means B047 and B010 together would need five names, so it would force me to drop Molenkamp or Mele or to cut Ye or Katori. That reopens exactly the allocation problem I am trying to avoid, and I would rather argue one part well than two parts with a compromised credit. I therefore do not propose it, but I would not block it if the majority wanted it and the three-name cap were somehow satisfied.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B051, would accept a trio that omits Mele in favour of Hasan, and says he would not oppose B047 if the attribution can be settled.
responses.response: I thank you for saying you would not oppose B047, and I hold my view on Mele. The chair records that Eriksson and Mehlig agree that the Z2 classification and the graphene quantum spin Hall proposal come from the Kane-Mele pair together, and replacing Mele with Hasan would reward the three-dimensional experiment while removing half of the original theory. If the committee wants to recognise Hasan, that belongs in a later three-dimensional part and not in a swap here. On B051 I accept your point that earlier prizes honoured observed phenomena before a full explanation, so the unsettled pairing mechanism is not fatal. I still place B051 below B047 because the first author of the 2018 experiments, Cao, lies outside the three names, and the credit seems less settled than for B047.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B010, treats the 2016 prize as a risk for topological insulators in the sense that it may already cover the territory, and says the committee might prefer to wait for the redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I take the 2016 risk seriously and have tried to meet it with a concrete distinction in my case against, namely that the 2016 prize concerned topological order and phase transitions in model systems and that B047 concerns a time-reversal-invariant, spin-orbit-driven phase observed in real materials without a magnetic field. If you do not find that sufficient, I would like to hear what part of the Z2 insulator you believe is already inside the 2016 citation. On waiting for the redefinition, I agree with Kroll and Lindroth that the science does not depend on it, so I do not see waiting as a reason to rank B010 lower, but I also do not see it as a reason to rank it higher. It is the same argument that applies in the other direction: B047 does not need to wait for anything either.

uncertainties: Whether Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang can be recognised in the citation wording or in the record without extending the names beyond three, and whether Molenkamp can carry the experimental credit for the two-dimensional observation alone.
Whether the three-dimensional topological insulator work of Hasan, Fu and Moore is better treated as a separate part in a later year.
Whether the 2016 prize leaves enough room for B047. I believe the Z2 insulator is distinct, but I have not checked this against the committee's earlier discussions.
Whether the committee will give a measurement-capability invention (B010) the same weight as a new organising concept (B047); this may decide the vote more than any question of fact.
My account of priority and of the roles of each group rests on my recollection of the literature and has not been verified against the supplied files.
statement.conflict_note: I direct the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and work at Chalmers with Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson, and I am a frequent co-author with Anton Frisk Kockum. This is a direct connection to B041 (circuit QED) and a looser one to B046 and other quantum-computing candidates through WACQT. I would recuse myself from any decision placing circuit QED in the prize, and I have removed B041 from my alternatives. Olsson's note that I am a Chalmers colleague is relevant to that check. No specific connection to B047 or B010 is apparent from my profile, and I make no claim of one.
